attributes.name: extend
attributes.digest: Index Outside Table Handling
attributes.description: Theattribute controls howresponds when an input index value (either signal or float) is less than zero or greater than the table size.

choices.label: Whenis Zero (0), a zero signal is output when the index is outside the table bounds.

choices.digest: Output lowest or highest table values
choices.label: Whenis set to Extend (1),outputs the value at index 0 is output when the input index less than zero. It outputs the value at the highest table index is when the input index is greater than the table size.
Whenis set to Wrap (2),performs a modulo operation on the input index. Example: if the table size is 128 and the input is 130, the value at index 2 (130 mod 128) will be output.
Whenis set to Ignore (3), any input index outside the table size is ignored and does not change the output.

attributes.name: inmap
attributes.digest: Input Scale to Table Index
attributes.description: Theattribute specifies a range of input samples to map to table indices. For instance if your input signal will be between 0 and 1, you can use anof, which will scale to the current size of the table. If the table changes size, the current input map adjusts automatically. To clear the current, use a value ofor.

attributes.name: inputmode
attributes.digest: Input Mode
attributes.description: Theattribute determines how input values produce output values.

choices.label: Whenis set to Lookup (0), an incoming value is used as an index into the table.
Whenis set to Increment Index (1), a change event in the input signal (according to the setting of theattribute) causes the table to output the value at the next index.

Whenis set to Random Distribution (2), a change event in the input signal (according to the setting of theattribute) causes the table to output a value based on using the table data as a probability distribution. See themessage for more details.

attributes.name: interp
attributes.digest: Interpolation Mode
attributes.description: Theattribute determines how input values between integer table indices produce output.

choices.label: Whenis set to None (0), an incoming value is truncated to its integer value before the lookup. No interpolation is performed.

Whenis set to Linear (1), the output for any input value between two table indices is linearly interpolated between the table values at those two indices. For example, an input of 1.5 -- with table values of 5 at index 1 and 10 at index 2 -- produces an output of 7.5.
Whenis set to Round (2), an incoming value is rounded to the nearest integer value before the lookup. No interpolation is performed.

attributes.name: triggermode
attributes.digest: Trigger Mode
attributes.description: Theattribute determines how input values are interpret as change events for triggering either an incremented index or random probability output according to the setting of theattribute. Whenis set to 0 (Lookup), theattribute has no effect and is disabled.

choices.label: Whenis set to Zero to Non-Zero (0), a non-zero sample value in the input that follows a zero sample value causes a change event to occur.
Whenis set to Change (1), a sample value in the input that differs from the previous value causes a change event to occur.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Double-clicking on aobject opens a window where you can edit the values of the lookup table.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: Themessage treats the table as a probability distribution and outputs a signal corresponding to a randomly chosen index within the table. A location in the table with a higher value is more likely to have its index selected.

messages.name: float
messages.description: When a signal is not connected to the inlet of, a number sets the index to use for table lookup output. If the number contains a fractional part andis set to Linear, the output will be interpolated between two table values. The number is also mapped to an index according to the current setting of theattribute and the table value is scaled according to theattribute.

messages.name: goto
messages.digest: Change index for prev and next messages
messages.description: The word, followed by a table index, sets the next table index used by either theormessages as they increment or decrement through the table. Unlike aor,itself does not change the output of theobject and its index is not modified by theattribute.

messages.name: next
messages.description: When a signal is not connected to the inlet of, themessage adds one to the most recent table index set by the, or, then causes theto output the value at this index as a signal. If amessage immediately preceded, the value at the specified index is output. Note thatdoes not force the table index to an integer value, so it preserves any fractional part of the index caused by a previousmessage. Whenincrements the index and it is larger than the table size, it wraps around to zero.

messages.name: prev
messages.description: When a signal is not connected to the inlet of, themessage subtracts one from the most recent table index set by the, or, then causes theto output the value at this index as a signal. If amessage immediately preceded, the value at the specified index is output. Note thatdoes not force the table index to an integer value, so it preserves any fractional part of the index caused by a previousmessage. Whendecrements the index and it becomes less than zero, it will wrap around to the end of the table.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: Incoming signal values are used as indices for table lookup.

inlets.description: Incoming signal values are used as indices for table lookup. If your input signal is not in the range of 0 to the table size, use theattribute to specify an input range to map to the entire size of the table. Note the indices are zero-relative so for a table of size 128 the indices range from 0 to 127.

outlets.description: Output signal values produced by table lookup. If you want to adjust the range of the table values (for example so they range from 0 to 1), use theattribute to specify an output range.
